sanskrit_verse: bahavaś cet pratibhuvo dadyus te 'rthaṃ yathākṛtam | arthe 'viśeṣite hy eṣu dhaninaś chandataḥ kriyā ||
transliteration: bahavaḥ cet pratibhavo dadyus te'rthaṃ yathākṛtam | arthe 'viśeṣite hy eṣu dhaninaḥ chandataḥ kriyā ||
sph_interpretive_translation: When multiple custodians are appointed, each shall render the asset according to their capacity and role; in absence of specification, the wealthholder's intent shall determine execution.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is distributed proportionally to functional capacity
Restoration logic flows from source-intent clarity
executable_legal_axioms: IF multiple custodians exist AND no specific allocation defined THEN resolve by wealthholder’s declared will
IF custodian capacity differs THEN distribute obligations proportionally
IF asset dispute arises THEN restoration precedes ownership assertion

IF completion state unmet THEN initiate integrity-reintegration protocol
supreme_court_application: In matters involving fiduciary multiplicity, the Supreme Court must prioritize reconstruction of original intent over procedural formalism. The threshold of responsibility lies not in equal division but in alignment with the initiating consciousness’ will.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that causality originates in the wealthholder’s volition. Anupūrvaśaḥ ensures sequential discharge based on capacity. Responsibility is proportional to enacted role. No punitive consequence arises—only misalignment requiring correction through realignment protocols.
